A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STI-Bench research and contain 19 complete, readable pages, including Appendices A–C. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v4 reports original evaluations of ten MLLMs on STI-Bench in Tables 2–3, error analysis in Section 4.3, and additional results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains these original model evaluations, error analyses, and appendix results.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, ground-truth computation, QA generation, human filtering, and distractor adjustment procedures in Section 3 and Appendices A–B are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Waymo, ScanNet, and Omni6DPose for the same outdoor, indoor, and desktop coverage and eight spatial-temporal tasks. The appendix categories and illustrated scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same ten evaluated MLLMs, and Tables 4–6 retain the same four-model comparison sets. No comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains uniform sampling of 30 frames, the 20-frame exception for Claude-3.7-Sonnet, sampling-FPS information in prompts, five answer choices, and direct accuracy evaluation. The stated model configurations and analysis sampling procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same Gemini-2.5-Pro error analysis and three principal error categories. Figures 6–7 and Appendix C preserve the same case studies and supplementary breakdowns.

E5.justification: Both versions report point accuracies without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No statistical or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All corresponding result entries, rankings, and findings in the main text and appendices are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports average accuracies of 41.4% for Gemini-2.5-Pro and 40.7% for Qwen2.5-VL-72B in both versions.

T1.justification: The task definitions, ground-truth equations in Appendix A, and distractor-adjustment mathematics in Section 3.2 and Appendix B are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and claims that current MLLMs struggle with precise spatial-temporal understanding, particularly quantitative measurement and motion analysis.

C2.justification: The explanations involving spatial quantification, temporal dynamics, and cross-modal grounding are unchanged. The same qualifications about model specialization and reliability for embodied AI and autonomous driving remain.

D1.justification: The documented data processing, annotation review, distractor settings, inference details, and project-access information are unchanged. The new funding acknowledgement adds no technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, benchmark positioning in Table 1, and all 52 reference entries are unchanged.

P1.justification: On page 9, v5 adds funding attribution to NSFC-62306046, changes 'Acknowledgements' to 'Acknowledgement', and lightly edits the thanks paragraph. The arXiv version stamp updates; the research narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 uses much higher-resolution versions of the same video frames, with minor typography, border, and spacing changes. The acknowledgement paragraph reflows locally; the remaining scientific figures, tables, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Figure 2's clearer imagery makes the benchmark illustrations easier to inspect, and page 9 now explicitly identifies the funding source. These provide modest gains in presentation and disclosure; the scientific content, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
